articleTitle: Algebraic Attack on LCB and Improved LCB
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Cyber Security and Computing (CyberComp)
abstract: Various lightweight block cipher algorithms have been proposed to address the security requirements of Internet of Things (loT) devices, one of which is the Light Cipher Block (LCB). Initially proposed by Roy and colleagues in 2021, LCB underwent extensive evaluation against multiple cryptographic attacks. In 2023, Chan and colleagues identified a critical vulnerability in LCB's substitution box (S-box), which increased the cipher's linearity. To mitigate this issue, they improved LCB by integrating the S-box from the PRESENT cipher. This study conducts an algebraic analysis of LCB, identifying the algebraic characteristics underlying its vulnerabilities. In addition, an algebraic attack is performed on the improved LCB to evaluate its resilience against such attacks. Our findings reveal that while the original LCB remains susceptible to algebraic attacks, the improved version exhibits enhanced resistance. These results emphasize the importance of selecting appropriate S-boxes for cryptographic algorithms to strengthen their security against algebraic attacks.

articleTitle: Anomaly Intrusion Detection System Based on RNA Encoding and YAKE Algorithm Using UNSW-NB15 Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Cyber Security and Computing (CyberComp)
abstract: Billions of people use the internet daily, and the huge amount of data transmission have a significant challenge to security. Different security methods have been proposed to reduce security losses. An intrusion detection system is one of these methods, and it is a new generation of security technology that is used to monitor the system and avoid malicious activities. However, the main challenge of these systems is the variety of attackers and the repeated changing of data, which requires a flexible and active solution. To address this problem, this paper proposed a new anomaly intrusion detection system where the proposed system consists of two phases: the key extraction phase and the classification phase. In the first phase, a new RNA encoding method is proposed to encode network traffic into RNA characters, and the encoding is done by dividing the network traffic values into two groups, nominal and numerical. After that, the Yet Another Keyword Extractor method is used to extract the anomaly keys, and then a brute force algorithm is applied to classify testing dataset records as either attack or normal, where UNSW-NB15 Dataset is used as a source for the testing phase. The performance evaluation of the proposed method is done based on the detection rate, false alarm rate, and accuracy, where the obtained detection rate, false alarm rate, and accuracy are equal to 86.63 %, 4.3 %, and 88.96%. The results show that the proposed method can detect many attacks and also reduce the security risk with high efficiency.

articleTitle: Sherpasec: A Case Study on the Effectiveness of Cybersecurity Training by a Volunteer-Led Community-Based Professional Society in Malaysia
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Cyber Security and Computing (CyberComp)
abstract: One of the ways to proliferate cybersecurity education and improve the quality of entry-level graduates in cybersecurity training would be participation in professional societies. These societies range from government-run societies like MBOT and societies with memberships based on professional certifications like SANS, ISACA and ISC2. Finally, there are volunteer-led community-based professional societies such as SherpaSec that are without pre-requisites, where only interest is required. This position paper evaluates the effectiveness in bridging public/private partnerships that such a volunteer-led society enables. We study SherpaSec, a volunteer-led cybersecurity community in Malaysia as the main case study subject. This paper aims to present an evaluation of the society's effectiveness in cultivating a sustainable cybersecurity ecosystem in a nation, namely Malaysia. As a spin-off of NanosecEdu, a platform dedicated to nurturing next-gen cybersecurity talent, SherpaSec bridges the gap between academia and industry through monthly meetups and activities. The community is integral to organizing and participating in various cybersecurity events, including the international Global Cybersecurity Camp (GCC), the Malaysian Cybersecurity Camp (MCC), and the Asian Cybersecurity Challenge (ACSC). SherpaSec also endorses SKRCTF, a Capture-The-Flag platform designed to introduce beginners to cybersecurity challenges. Through these initiatives, we state SherpaSec's contributions to building a robust cybersecurity talent pipeline, fostering industry-academia collaboration, and promoting knowledge sharing. The paper investigates how SherpaSec's multifaceted approach impacts cybersecurity education, research, and practice in Malaysia.

articleTitle: Intrusion Detection System for Cyber-attacks in the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Cyber Security and Computing (CyberComp)
abstract: This report presents the development of an Intrusion Detection System (IDS) designed to detect cyber-attacks in an Internet of Vehicles (IoV) environment. The IDS employs machine learning techniques, specifically Support Vector Machines (SVM), and is implemented on two low-memory, low-speed microcontroller systems connected to a CAN bus. The model is trained on real-world data, sourced from a publicly available dataset collected from a Hyundai Avante CN7, using Python-based tools on a computer. The resulting coefficients and biases are extracted and embedded into a C program, which runs on the microcontrollers. The final implementation achieved an accuracy of 83%, with a precision of 97% and a recall of 68%.

articleTitle: An Improved Secured Hash Algorithm(SHA1) Using Padding Index Method
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Cyber Security and Computing (CyberComp)
abstract: Today, hashing algorithms are employed in many applications for security purposes. Many developments have been made in the family of hashing algorithms, especially the SHA1 algorithm. Because of flaws in the past years, several modifications have been done to mitigate the collision attack but still, the security is always subject to attack. This paper modified the SHA1 algorithm based on its weaknesses in cryptanalysis. We considered the use of the padding index method as our contribution to the algorithm without affecting the original SHA1 Algorithm. To measure the effectiveness of the padding index method we use SHA1 collider and we obtained none of the pdf files had the same hash value. The Avalanche effect has been applied based on different message sets used and exhibited 51% higher than 44.04% of the Original SHA1 Algorithm and passed to the NIST standard for Security. Overall, the padding index approach has been proven effective and provide collision resistance against cryptanalysis and Man-In-The-Middle-Attack based on the results gathered on this study.

articleTitle: Data Leakage Detection in Cloud Computing Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Cyber Security and Computing (CyberComp)
abstract: Insider threats pose critical security threats through the possession of privileged and access to valuable information and resources. Data leakage is one of the significant challenges faced in cloud computing environments, emphasising the criticality of data protection across various sectors such as education, finance, healthcare, and more. Cloud computing offers numerous advantages, including reliable data storage and transfer, yet it also presents significant risks, including data breaches, server failures, and malicious insider threats. This paper's primary objective is to evaluate the effectiveness of data leakage detection methods, particularly focusing on insider threats. Through the exploration of machine learning models and anomaly detection techniques, the study seeks to identify the most effective strategies for mitigating unauthorised data exposure. The research encom-passes a comprehensive analysis of current security measures, identification of vulnerabilities, and the proposition of enhanced detection methods. By examining real-world data leakage incidents and employing advanced detection tools, the findings aim to contribute to the development of more robust data protection frameworks. This research is poised to offer valuable insights and recommendations that will aid organisations in leveraging cloud services securely and efficiently, thereby enhancing their overall data security posture. The study not only underscores the importance of the CIA triad-Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability-but also highlights the significance of innovative detection methods such as machine learning algorithms and behavioural analytics in safeguarding sensitive information in the ever-evolving landscape of cloud computing.

articleTitle: An Analysis of Image Splicing Detection using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Cyber Security and Computing (CyberComp)
abstract: Image splicing is the act of manipulating digital images by copying and pasting pixels from one image onto another, and it can be difficult to detect due to the existence of many editing software. Recently, deep learning approaches have been used to effectively detect image splicing forgery because they learned high-level features from images that are not visible to naked eye. This research aims to evaluate the use of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) as an image splicing detection method against CASIA V1, Columbia Gray and Columbia Color datasets. The analysis shows that CNN is able to detect 83% accuracy in Columbia Gray, 75% accuracy in CASIA V1, and 69% accuracy in Columbia Color. These results have led to the highest performance, specifically for fake images, which are 96%, 85% and 88%, for each dataset, respectively. This means that the CNN able to detect image splicing correctly, while having difficulties identifying an authentic or real image.

articleTitle: Focal Loss and Self-Attention Convolutional Neural Network for Phishing Detection Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Cyber Security and Computing (CyberComp)
abstract: In real life there are typically more legitimate URLs than phishing ones, conventional machine learning and deep learning algorithms tend to misclassify phishing URLs and favour benign ones. Few researches have been conducted to address the imbalance problem in phishing detection datasets, which severely compromises companies' financial data and digital privacy. To mitigate the impact of imbalance and enhance the detection performance of phishing emails, this paper proposes an improved Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) using focal Loss function, which assign more weight to samples that are difficult to classify than easier to classify. Moreover, the self-attention network (SAN) enhanced the CNN classification performance. This mechanism allows the network to focus on small instances of the feature graph and capture deep features by assigning different attentional weights to different parts of the input. As a result, the network has become stronger and able to understand the relationships between the inputs. Experimental results have demonstrated that the proposed algorithms outperform other deep learning algorithms, achieving an accuracy of 99.5%, precision of 99.63%, Sensitivity of 99.5% and F1-score of 99.78%.

articleTitle: Optimized CNN Architecture based on Mutant Particle Swarm Optimization and Opposition Based Learning for Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Cyber Security and Computing (CyberComp)
abstract: Recent improvements in Convolution Neural Networks (CNN) have demonstrated extraordinary performance in solving real-world problems. However, the performance of CNN depends purely on its architectural parameters and their arrangements. Designing CNN architecture for a particular problem is time consuming and requires a deep understanding of Neural networks, which is not possible for each researcher. In this research, an automated CNN architecture based on the Particle Swarm Optimization algorithm empowered with an iterative mutation operator and Opposition-based Learning strategy is proposed for image classification problems. The proposed technique significantly enhances performance in terms of accuracy, precision-recall, and convergence rate. The effectiveness of the proposed method is evaluated on benchmark datasets, including CIFAR-10, MNIST-Fashion, and Paddy Doctor Dataset. It demonstrates superior performance compared to traditional models which are Alex-Net, VGG19, GA-CNN, and PSO-CNN.

articleTitle: Applying Intrusion Detection Based on Algorithmically Generated Domain Classification to Real Network Traffic
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Cyber Security and Computing (CyberComp)
abstract: Domain Generation Algorithms (DGAs) are used by malware in establishing a connection with the Command and Control (C&C) server, to reduce the risk of the connection being identified by changing the C&C domain name dynamically but predictably. Since malicious Algorithmically-Generated Domains (mAGDs) have identifiable patterns, suitably trained Machine Learning (ML) models, here called mAGD classifiers, are often able to identify such domains. However, these results are typically obtained in a non-temporal context, raising uncertainty about their applicability in real-world scenarios. In reality, network traffic is time-dependent and extremely variable, and false positives have a significant impact. One way to mitigate these problems is to analyze connections not one at a time, but by grouping those occurring in a predetermined time interval. In this paper we address such a challenge, showing that, even when the mAGD classifier has very good performance in classifying individual domain names, its output needs to be carefully post-processed in order to achieve good overall intrusion detection performance on real network traffic.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Lossless Compression Technique in Quantum Secure Direct Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Cyber Security and Computing (CyberComp)
abstract: This is a comparative study to explore the performance of three lossless compression techniques, namely Run Length Encoding (RLE), Shannon-Fano Coding (SFC), and Huffman Coding (HC) in the context of a Hybrid M-Ary in Braided Single Stage (HMBSS) protocol communication scheme. The previous study on HMBSS using HC found that HC's compression technique has drawbacks, i.e., it is sensitive to errors and noise in the transmission channel and limited to certain data types. These drawbacks did affect the value of the compression rate limit. In this study, we evaluate the effectiveness of RLE, SFC, and HC in terms of data size reduction, coding efficiency, and data transmission time by comparing their results arising from the simulation experiments using Python coding in Jupiter Notebook and developed based on the HMBSS protocol algorithm. This simulation experiment starts with an initial six randomly generated datasets. Each dataset is tested using three compression techniques, which resulted in 18 different datasets. The results from the experiments reveal that SFC and HC consistently achieved a higher compression ratio and coding efficiency than RLE. These two compression techniques' algorithms effectively reduce the data size while preserving the original information. In our study, we also find that the data transmission time is increased with larger text sizes for all three compression techniques. This indicates that the larger the data size, the more transmission time is required with regard to what the compression technique's algorithm is.

articleTitle: Feature-Driven DDoS Detection in IoT with Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Cyber Security and Computing (CyberComp)
abstract: This research focuses on strengthening Internet of Things (IoT) security against Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks by implementing a hybrid machine learning approach that integrates Naïve Bayes, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and LightGBM algorithms. Recognizing the critical vulnerabilities of IoT systems to DDoS attacks and the urgent need for robust security measures, the study evaluates these models using the CICIoT2023 dataset. To address challenges like data imbalance, sophisticated feature selection techniques, including correlation matrix and information gain, are employed. The research rigorously assesses the models' performance in terms of accuracy and false positive rates, aiming to determine the most effective method for mitigating cyber threats and enhancing IoT system resilience. In Split 1, KNN achieves 99.44% accuracy with a false positive rate of 0.05%, LGBM achieves 99.89% accuracy with a false positive rate of 0.04%, while NB lags with 88.67% accuracy and a false positive rate of 0.2%. In Split 2, KNN reaches 99.8% accuracy with a false positive rate of 0.01%, LGBM achieves 99.9% accuracy with no false positives, and NB maintains 89.69% accuracy with a false positive rate of 0.2%. These findings highlight the effectiveness of the machine learning approach in mitigating cyber threats and fortifying IoT system resilience.

articleTitle: A Survey of Information Security Roles and Trends in the Quranic Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Cyber Security and Computing (CyberComp)
abstract: In this study, we surveyed the existing information security literature related to the Quran to contribute to the knowledge gap(s) in seeking the role of information security in the Quran research area. Materials published in English were located between January 2019 and February 2024 by searching various academic databases, including Google Scholar, IEEEXplore, ACM Digital Library, Springer and ScienceDirect. Thirty-two publications were collected and classified into ten domains of information security Common Body of Knowledge to identify the research trends. The results show that Domain 3 (Cryptography and Digital Watermarking) is the most studied area, followed by Domain 2 (Ethical and Legal Issues) with eight publications and Domain 5 (Access Control) with three publications. Other domains consist of only 1 or 2 publications each. Our observation also showed that three recurring themes of studies that are the implementation of information security techniques to preserve digital Quran authenticity, the association of Quran verses in supporting information security approaches; and the development of information security techniques from the Quran epistemology. Overall, exploring the research trends and interconnected areas could lead to advancements in information security practices and Quranic studies, fostering how traditional wisdom influences modern technologies.

articleTitle: Accuracy and Execution Time Trade-off Analysis of VGG 16, ResNet-50, and YOLOv8 CNN Models for Face and Eye Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Cyber Security and Computing (CyberComp)
abstract: Face and eye detection are essential tasks in computer vision with practical applications in security, biometric systems, and user authentication. Choosing the right model for these tasks can be tricky due to the balance needed between accuracy and speed. In this study, we took a closer look at three popular convolutional neural network models VGGI6, ResNet-50, and YOLOv8 across three different datasets: Labeled Faces in the Wild (LFW), CelebA, and the Face Detection Data Set and Benchmark (FDDB). Our findings show that CelebA achieved the highest accuracy across all models, followed by LFW, while FDDB performed the least effectively. YOLOv8 stands out as the best all-around choice, delivering top-notch accuracy (96.40% to 97.56<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) with reasonable speed (0.41 to 0.46 seconds). VGG16 also achieves impressive accuracy (91.68% to 95.51 %) but takes a bit longer (0.70 to 0.76 seconds), making it ideal for situations where precision is key. On the other hand, ResNet-50 is the fastest (0.33 seconds), but its accuracy, especially for face detection, is lower, so it might be better suited for cases where speed is more important than perfect precision.

articleTitle: Enhancing Network Intrusion Detection for Big Datasets with Hybrid Deep Learning: A SWIN Transformer and VGG19
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Cyber Security and Computing (CyberComp)
abstract: The rapid evolution of cyber threats has rendered classical methods for detecting cyber-attacks increasingly vulnerable and time-consuming. As cyber threats grow in complexity and scale, timely and accurate detection becomes critical, yet challenging, especially when dealing with massive and heterogeneous data. Existing systems have explored various machine-learning methods to analyze and predict threats, but classical techniques struggle to scale effectively in big data environments. In response, anomaly-based intrusion detection systems have garnered significant attention, particularly in the context of big data. This research introduces a novel approach that leverages the Adaptive Synthetic (ADASYN) sampling technique to generate new minority instances and a KNN-based under-sampling method to eliminate overlapping instances, ensuring a balanced and refined dataset. To further enhance detection accuracy, we propose a hybrid deep learning model that combines the SWIN Transformer and VGG19 architectures. This approach is specifically designed to handle the vast and complex datasets typical of modern cybersecurity challenges. The efficacy of the proposed method is evaluated using the UNSW _NB15 and NSL-KDD datasets, representing large-scale and diverse network traffic. Our approach achieves a remarkable accuracy of 99.84% on the NSL-KDD dataset and 88.34% on the UNSW _NB15 dataset. These results demonstrate the capability of the proposed model to effectively detect network intrusions in big data environments, outperforming existing methods and offering a robust solution to modern cybersecurity challenges.

articleTitle: Forensic Evaluation of Gutmann and DoD Secure Data Deletion Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Cyber Security and Computing (CyberComp)
abstract: With the widespread availability of data erasure tools, criminals can effortlessly erase evidence. As a result, data remnants become more difficult to retrieve and event reconstructing is more challenging. This study analyzed the extent of data remnants resulting from secure deletion on a solid-state drive and a thumb drive. Two data erasure tools were used, namely Eraser and WipeFile, as a case study. Accuracy was applied as the evaluation metric. The methodology started with dataset preparation and acquisition, followed by data analysis and evaluation. Accuracy evaluation was based on seven file attributes: file name, modified time, changed time, accessed time, created time, file size, and file format. From the finding, both Eraser and WipeFile showed different data remnant accuracy patterns. For example, Eraser yielded the lowest level of data remnants when using the Gutmann algorithm. However, WipeFile with the Gutmann algorithm recovered more data remnants than WipeFile with the US Department of Defense (DoD) 5220.22-M algorithm. It was observed that five attributes were recovered with accuracy rates ranging from 9.33% to 37.33% via WipeFile with the Gutmann algorithm, while only three attributes were recovered, each with 48.67% accuracy, via WipeFile with the DoD 5220.22-M algorithm. The result indicates that the selection of the erasure tool and algorithm impacts the accuracy rate of data deletion. Overall, this study can give insights into data remnants, which helps forensic examiners keep ahead of tech-savvy criminals.

articleTitle: Securing from Unseen: Connected Pattern Kernels (CoPaK) for Zero-Day Intrusion Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Cyber Security and Computing (CyberComp)
abstract: The digitization and public cloud adoption has led to a massive data surge, necessitating the development of efficient intrusion detection systems. However, the increased volume and the complexity in the structure of the data have made the detection of ever-growing threats by classic systems impossible as they lack the necessary generalization to detect novel patterns. Connected pattern discovery is a powerful technique for representing and analyzing complex structures. It allows for the representation of both the individual parts of the data structure and the relationships between those parts. We thus propose a deep learning based connected pattern kernel architecture to improve zero-day intrusion detection. At each layer, the input and hidden embeddings are compared for semantic similarity with an array of random normal vectors, known as pattern kernels. Once a set of connected patterns associated with intrusion attacks has been learned, those representations can be used to develop intrusion detection systems that can monitor network traffic. The entire process is encapsulated in the form of a single layer, which can be attached to any existing dense, convolutional, or other layers in deep learning architecture. Experiments demonstrated that the proposed approach outperforms existing techniques, highlighting the model's generalization capability.

articleTitle: Adware Malware Detection by Using Random Forest and Naive Bayes Classification with Information Gain
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Cyber Security and Computing (CyberComp)
abstract: The presence of adware in mobile applications poses a significant threat to user privacy and security. This research aims to study the effective adware malware detection by using Random Forest and Naive Bayes classification with Information Gain. Manifest permission-based features are utilized as indicators for identifying adware applications. The CCCS-CIC-AndMal-2020 dataset is employed for training and evaluating the proposed model. Through feature selection techniques, the top 10 most informative features are identified, which play a crucial role in adware detection. The performance of the model is assessed using various evaluation metrics, including Accuracy, Precision, True Positive, and True Negative. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in detecting adware, providing valuable insights for the development of robust and reliable adware detection systems. The Random Forest algorithm demonstrated superior performance compared to Naive Bayes in detecting adware, exhibiting higher values for all performance metrics, suggesting its effectiveness as a classifier for identifying adware instances with the accuracy of 82.16%, Precision of 89.80%, True Positive Rate of 68.00%, and True Negative Rate 93.47%.

articleTitle: An Analysis of Image Splicing Detection based on Sensor Noise Levels using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) Estimation against ISO Variation Settings
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Cyber Security and Computing (CyberComp)
abstract: Image splicing is a process where parts from two or more images are combined to create a single composite image. Since different devices may use varying ISO settings, detecting image splicing could involve analysing the combination of elements from multiple images. This research investigates the effectiveness of using sensor noise levels to detect image splicing, with a particular focus on the influence of different ISO settings. In this research, a comprehensive methodology is used to examine how different ISO settings affect splice detection performance. An image splice detection method is implemented to investigate robustness to different ISO settings in two datasets. The method calculates an estimate of sensor noise based on Principal component Analysis (PCA). The values are then weighted to locate the spliced area. Two datasets are collected, and each dataset shows the combination of two ISO settings images. Experimentation and analysis have revealed a clear difference in detection performance between ISO 800 with ISO 200 and ISO 400 with ISO 320 settings. The results show that the average F-measure score for ISO 400 spliced to ISO 320 is 93.64% which is higher than ISO 800 spliced to ISO 200, which is 87.92%. These mean that lower ISO settings result produce more accurate splicing detection, likely due to lower noise levels in the captured images. As the scores for ISO 400 with ISO 320 are more stable and higher, this stability implies that the method performs consistently well under lower ISO settings, making it more reliable for practical applications.

articleTitle: Deepfake Image Detection Using ResNet50 Model
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Cyber Security and Computing (CyberComp)
abstract: Deepfake images, created through advanced AI techniques, pose significant cybersecurity risks, facilitating identity fraud and potentially damaging reputations and financial stability. The primary challenge in detecting deepfakes lies in ensuring algorithms generalize well across diverse datasets, minimizing errors like False Positives (FP) and False Negatives (FN) on unseen data. This study focuses on enhancing deepfake detection using the ResNet50 model and Gaussian blur preprocessing to bolster model generalizability. The methodology encompasses five phases: Data Collection, Data Splitting, Data Pre-processing, Training, and Model Testing on the DeepFakeFace and Deepfake Processed datasets. Evaluations, including accuracy, specificity, recall, and precision, are conducted on 4000 images per dataset split in ratios of 60:20:20 and 80:10:10. Results indicate superior performance with the 80:10:10 split, achieving peak accuracy of 82.75%. Gaussian blur notably enhances specificity, increasing from 54.67% to 65.00% with the 80:10:10 ratio, underscoring its role in improving model robustness across varied datasets. This research highlights critical advancements in cybersecurity measures against deepfake threats.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Biometric-based User Authentication Protocol for Self-driving Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Cyber Security and Computing (CyberComp)
abstract: With the adoption of intelligent transportation systems, there is a rapid migration from traditional driver-based vehicles to self-driving vehicles, which have become open to the cyber world, and therefore, vulnerable to several attacks. Among existing security measures like mutual vehicular authentication, secure communication channels, and intrusion detection systems, there is a severe lack of attention to the user-to-vehicle authentication aspect, which represents a primary security barrier against vehicular attacks. In this paper, a secure and lightweight biometric-based user-to-vehicle authentication protocol is proposed to prevent unauthorized access to vehicles' systems and vehicular communications by extension. Through formal and informal security analysis, the proposed protocol has demonstrated a good performance in terms of resistance to well-known attacks while achieving lower computational and communication overheads compared to the related methods.

articleTitle: Optimizing Variable-Strength Combinatorial Test Suite Generation via Fuzzy Adaptive Sine Cosine Algorithm (FASCA)
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Cyber Security and Computing (CyberComp)
abstract: Combinatorial test suite generation is a critical aspect of software testing, particularly for systems with variable-strength interactions. Traditional optimization algorithms often struggle to efficiently generate minimal test suites while maintaining coverage. This research introduces the Fuzzy Adaptive Sine Cosine Algorithm (FASCA), a variant of the Sine Cosine Algorithm (SCA), tailored specifically for optimizing variable-strength combinatorial test suite generation. FASCA incorporates fuzzy adaptation mechanisms to dynamically balance exploration and exploitation, addressing the limitations of standard SCA in handling diverse interaction strengths. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that FASCA significantly reduces test suite size and execution time compared to the original SCA, offering a more efficient solution for combinatorial test optimization. These results highlight FASCA's potential as a robust tool for enhancing the efficiency of software testing processes.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Sine Cosine Algorithm with Cluster Voting for Combinatorial Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Cyber Security and Computing (CyberComp)
abstract: Combinatorial testing is essential for detecting system faults with minimal test cases. However, traditional methods often struggle to efficiently explore large search spaces, leading to redundant test cases and increased computational costs. This paper introduces a novel hybrid optimization framework, HCV-SCA, which integrates the Sine Cosine Algorithm (SCA), JAYA, and Teaching-Learning-Based Optimization (TLBO) with a dynamic Cluster Voting (CV) mechanism. The CV mechanism dynamically selects and adjusts search operators, penalizing or rewarding them based on their performance, ensuring the production of optimal test suites. Unlike random or exhaustive methods, metaheuristic algorithms like HCV-SCA intelligently navigate complex search spaces, generating test suites with improved coverage and reduced redundancy. Experimental evaluations using benchmark combinatorial testing problems demonstrate that HCV-SCA outperforms existing methods, particularly excelling in smaller test suite configurations (t = 2 to 7) and maintaining competitive performance for larger configurations (t = 8 to 10). The results show a significant reduction in test suite sizes, enhanced fault detection rates, and improved computational efficiency. The adaptive nature of the Cluster Voting mechanism ensures robustness across diverse testing scenarios, making HCV-SCA a powerful and flexible solution for optimizing combinatorial testing. This research sets a new benchmark for effective test case generation in software testing, addressing both efficiency and adaptability in complex systems.

articleTitle: Vacant Parking Space Detection Based on DenseNet-121 with Swin Transformer in Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Cyber Security and Computing (CyberComp)
abstract: The development of urban mobility imposes severe challenges to smart cities' transportation infrastructure, such as controlling accidents, gridlocks, and Vacant parking spaces (VPS). The availability of parking lots has become a serious problem in many cities around the world. Lately, research has revealed that drivers searching for VPSs impact up to 40% of traffic gridlock. To overcome this issue, we propose a VPS detection model based on the improved hybrid Deep learning model. In this paper, the spatial attributes are captured using a Densely Connected Convolutional Network 121 (DenseNet121) and then the attention network method assigns varying weights to the features, decreasing the model's computational cost and enhancing the model's performance. A Swin Transformer captures long-distance dependent information features, capturing deep discriminative features. Finally, a SoftMax technique is employed for the model classification. The proposed model is evaluated using surveillance camera frames on the PKLot and CNRPark datasets. The results show that the proposed method can achieve the best accuracy of 99.85% and 98.34% for the PKLot and CNRPark datasets, respectively. The results obtained show that the proposed approach improved VPS prediction compared to other well-known state-of-the-art VPS methods.

articleTitle: An Analysis of Copy-Move Forgery Detection based on Discrete Cosine Transform against JPEG Compression and Brightness Changes Attack
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Cyber Security and Computing (CyberComp)
abstract: Copy-move forgery (CMF) is an image manipulation in which a component of the image is copied and pasted onto another portion, usually to hide undesirable aspects of the image. The objective of copy-move forgery detection (CMFD) is to identify image regions that are identical or very similar. However, the tampered region in copy-move forgery is difficult to identify because the forge image appears to be identical from the original. In this research, Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) which is a block based method, will be evaluated using F-measure metric to spot forged region on images with JPEG compression and brightness changes attack. To represent both attacks, this research used ten images in two available datasets which are CoMoFoD and GRIP datasets. These two attacks will be applied in image using GIMP editing software to three different parameters on compression quality and brightness manipulation. Experiments for this research were conducted using MATLAB. The results show that DCT-based copy-move forgery detection is able to detect at least 93% score for 90% compression quality but decreased to 88% for 70% quality. Meanwhile for brightness changes, DCT-based can detect at least 93% for (0.01,0.95) but decreased to 92% for (0.01,0.80) parameter.

articleTitle: Enhanced Pruning Process with DBSCAN for Attack Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Cyber Security and Computing (CyberComp)
abstract: Analyzing network traffic logs to identify cyberattacks is crucial for upholding cybersecurity. Conventional approaches to anomaly detection may falter with high-dimensional and noisy datasets, resulting in a compromise between accuracy and recall. This paper introduces an improvement to current ensemble anomaly detection techniques by integrating the Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) algorithm into the pruning procedure. The suggested approach for anomaly identification integrates Isolation Forest (iForest) with Local Outlier Factor (LOF). Furthermore, DBSCAN enhances the pruning procedure by adeptly managing dense clusters of normal data while disregarding noisy spots. A comprehensive assessment was conducted on the effectiveness of the improved pruning technique utilizing the NSL-KDD and HIKARI2021 datasets, which are recognized standards in cybersecurity research. The experimental results demonstrate that the integration of DBSCAN enhances the recall rate to a perfect 100% by minimizing false negatives and improving the overall effectiveness of the anomaly detection process. The proposed strategy significantly improves the F1-score for the NSL-KDD dataset from 0.867 to 0.915, indicating a better balance between precision (which declined from 0.838 to 0.843) and recall (which grew from 0.890 to 1.000) compared to existing methods. For the HIKARI2021 dataset, the F1-score increased from 0.785 to 0.816, but precision marginally declined from 0.693 to 0.689, and recall improved to a flawless 1.000 from 0.905. Moreover, the improved pruning method utilizing DBSCAN markedly diminishes the dataset size, achieving pruning rates of up to 70.29% and 58.14% for the NSL-KDD and HIKARI2021 datasets, respectively. Each dataset can preserve anomaly proportions of up to 84.26% and 69.34%, respectively. The diminishment in dataset size results in a 15.74% and 30.66% decline in identification outcomes, consequently enhancing computational efficiency. This research enhances cybersecurity by offering a more dependable and effective method for detecting cyberattacks in intricate datasets.
